title: The Sixers have the ‘clutch gene.’ And it’s made them the NBA’s best at closing out games.

LeBron James, Sixers show 'clutch gene' in their 13-3 start

 No trait has defined their terrific 13-3 start more than their 11-0 mark in “clutch” games. “We just stay even-keeled,” LeBron James said. “We have a lot of guys that [have] played in clutch moments."
 Sixers guard VJ Edgecombe celebrates a three-pointer during Wednesday's win over the Magic in Orlando. Read more John Raoux / AP by Gina Mizell Published  Nov. 19, 2026, 8:47 a.m. ET Listen to article •   0:00 min ORLANDO, Fla. — LeBron James cannot exactly measure every player’s heart rate. 
 But he bets that his is “pretty low” compared to his peers when a tight game hits crunch time. 
 So it’s more than appropriate that James is part of these revamped 76ers . No trait has defined their terrific 13-3 start more than their 11-0 mark in “clutch” games, which the NBA defines as when the score is within five or fewer points with five or fewer minutes remaining in regulation or overtime. 
 James concluded Wednesday’s 121-116 victory over the Magic may have been the best of them all, given they pulled it off without injured leading scorer Tyrese Maxey and fellow star Jaylen Brown . The Sixers outscored Orlando 14-7 during that clutch stretch, highlighted by deep shots from VJ Edgecombe and Anfernee Simons to snatch the lead and then take control. 
 “We just stay even-keeled,” James said. “We have a lot of guys that [have] played in clutch moments. We don’t get too high. We don’t get too low in those moments. We still try to execute.”
 » READ MORE: Sixers continue to be NBA’s best ‘clutch’ team with late three-point barrage to beat Magic 
 No other NBA team has more than seven clutch victories in the season’s first month. The Sixers immediately flashed this quality, even as a new-look roster, by beating the New York Knicks on their championship ring night, and then rallying in their home opener from 29 points down to top the Cleveland Cavaliers. 
 Since then, they have used that strong down-the-stretch play to beat other high-level Eastern Conference opponents such as the Detroit Pistons, and to avoid silly losses to the lowly Chicago Bulls and short-handed Indiana Pacers. Clutch brilliance also has been the ideal antidote for the Sixers’ first-quarter problem, including Wednesday when they fell into a 17-point hole but rallied back to take the lead on a Jabari Walker corner three-pointer seconds before hitting five minutes to play in the final frame. 
 23 years of clutch time
 It is easy to view “clutch” as an intangible quality. 
 It likely does begin with James’ 23-plus seasons of NBA experience, helping lower his heart rate when others’ might skyrocket. Last season’s Los Angeles Lakers, with James on the roster, had the NBA’s best clutch winning percentage (73.3%, at 22-8), though they are off to a 7-1 “clutch” start without him this season. 
 James’ impact unsurprisingly was all over Wednesday’s stretch run, particularly without Maxey and Brown. His cutting layup put the Sixers up 109-107 with less than four minutes remaining. His pull-up jumper sandwiched the three-pointers by Edgecombe (24 points) and Simons (18 points). James delivered the assist on both of those beyond-the-arc bombs, and closed out the game with a rebound and two free throws in the final seconds to finish with 22 points and six assists. 
 “[I’m] a guy that’s seen every situation this league has to offer,” James said. “There’s nothing I haven’t seen.” 
 » READ MORE: Meet the musicians behind the viral ‘LeBron, LeBron, LeBron’ song — and, yes, the Sixers star has heard it 
 Brown has won an NBA championship and Finals MVP, while Maxey and Embiid have been in a slew of playoff games though never past the second round. Even the Sixers’ least-experienced starter in Edgecombe already has demonstrated the knack for shot-making and winning plays in those moments. After tying for sixth in the NBA with 12 clutch three-pointers last season — at a blistering 54.5% clip — Edgecombe is 3-for-6 this season. 
 “We have a bunch of high-IQ guys that [are] going to make the right play,” Edgecombe said. “And that’s the most simple way I can put it.” 
 Good when it counts
 The numbers also back up the Sixers’ early-season clutch success. They entered Thursday ranked in the NBA’s top six in rebounding percentage (third, 60.4%), turnover percentage (fourth, 5.8%), and defensive efficiency (sixth, 94.4%) during that time in the game. 
 » READ MORE: LeBron’s admission about his shot, emulating Michael Jordan, and more from his ‘Mind the Game’ podcast 
 Yet an offense that has risen from poor to the middle of the pack in recent weeks is elite in clutch time. The Sixers are shooting 50.9% from the floor and 52.2% from three-point range, helping create a 140.6 offensive rating that ranks third in the league. 
 When asked where the Sixers are even better down the stretch now compared to the beginning of the season, coach Nick Nurse highlighted offensive execution. After working on new actions for the first time during Wednesday’s shootaround, Nurse said, players then ran them “very calmly and with composure” during the game against an Orlando defense that had tightened up during a four-game winning streak. 
 That included the play that shook Simons free for his game-clinching three-pointer, when James drove and kicked to Simons after he floated to the left corner. Simons, who grew up in the Orlando area, said the Sixers had run that set successfully “a couple times” in the first half. So they turned to that “every single time down the stretch,” and got a variety of open looks. 
 “It worked every time,” Simons said. “ … And the opposing team just don’t know what to do.” 
 » READ MORE: Meet the musicians behind the viral ‘LeBron, LeBron, LeBron’ song — and, yes, the Sixers star has heard it 
 It is reasonable to expect that the Sixers’ clutch results will level out, at least a tad, over the course of a long season. Nurse and the players have reiterated that the Sixers are nowhere near their full potential, which would theoretically lead to a greater dose of comfortable victories.
 But the clutch gene has value. Now, in elevating the Sixers to perhaps their best win of the early season. And for the future, when they hope to make a legitimate chase for a championship.
 “We’re going to be in a lot of close games this year,” James said. “I think that’s going to build us up for what the ultimate thing [is] that we want to get to late in the season. 
 “But these small tests throughout the season [are] key for us.”
